videos.title: Introduction to "My Journey" discussion series
videos.text: hi everyone i wanted to make a quick uh introduction video um to introduce both myself and my purpose for doing this interview series with julie dasa so as some of you may know i'm juno and i've been a student of chula dasa for about three years now and like many of you i was introduced to him through his book the mind illuminated and then being really impressed by it and really enjoying the method and starting up a practice of my own i applied to be in a teacher training program to which i was accepted and it kind of all went from there and a few months ago i reached out to chula dasa and came up proposed to him that we do this interview series so i've always really enjoyed reading hagiographies and stories about people's spiritual journeys and there are a number of good ones that i'm going to recommend to you now if you are interested in this and just to give you an idea of what inspired me to do these videos um so there are several about the life of the buddha such as by karen armstrong or bhikkhu anglio and then there's a wonderful compilation called the disciples of the buddha which i can really really recommend it's fantastically written and it's very accessible now the problem with these sorts of ones and um is that they're so ancient that the stories are very difficult to pick apart from myth and legend and of course naturally these stories have been mixed in with those things as time has passed and and stories were passed on so i've also really enjoyed reading contemporary accounts of spiritual journeys and awakening and uh some wonderful ones that i've read were i give you my life by ayakema she was a german jew who escaped the holocaust and then went on to lead a very exciting life adventuring and exploring around the world with her family before becoming a buddhist nun and a renowned teacher of the jhānas and i think she she started seriously or she became a nun seriously started practicing in her 50s then there's a book by jack caulfield called living dharma which is about 12 buddhist masters people like mahasi sayador and arjun chah and it's fantastic each one of them tells their life story and uh also their methods and their their particular flavor of of buddhist practice there's one that's uh less well-known uh called a record of awakening by uh aloka a man named david smith who was an english man who worked as a gardener his whole life but also meditated and traversed the stages of awakening and eventually went on to be a teacher as well one of my favorite accounts is a book about the life of dipa ma an indian woman who suffered greatly and and suffered great tragedy in her family was a widow and lost some of her children died and and yet she became an acknowledged and highly realized and compassionate compassionate buddhist teacher uh despite these humble beginnings and if you have any suggestions for fantastic books like that that i haven't mentioned here please leave them in the comments below i'd love to take a look as i said i really enjoy these kinds of books anyway overall the point most people come into meditation and dharma practice like many of the people i've just mentioned because they've had intimate experiences of suffering and the unsteadiness of life tragedy loss pain heartbreak grief and death and generally it is not people who are satisfied or content with their lives that seek out this kind of training so in other interviews that chula dasa has done over the years and i recommend the ones uh he's done with uh michael taft or guru viking i'm sure there are others that i'm not thinking of now but um he's uh talked about snippets about his own traumatic childhood and other problems such as uh difficult marriages and facing serious illness uh but he's never told the whole story in such a way that we can learn from his experiences and apart from a few references in tmi to his own struggles in his meditative journey we didn't get to know much about john at all in that book uh i know the the newer edition has an introduction which has a bit more um information in it but really we don't know what you know stage three was like for him or what uh stream entry was like for him and uh because of this lack of of knowledge about our teachers we often start thinking about them as super human gurus or or near perfect beings which is a huge mistake it is after all uh only through uh these very human experiences of of failure and and pain and missteps that um they learnt and that we really learn and grow and change so these interviews are an opportunity for john yates to talk about how he became chula dasa and more importantly to share his life experiences warts and all so that we can learn from them and specifically that anyone no matter what difficulties they experience be it trauma or mental illness or disease uh can benefit from ultimately being free from their suffering so my intention here was to let chula dasa tell his story in his own way in as much detail as as he is comfortable doing and then connect his life story and events to his path of practice and spiritual growth development and and realization after looking at his life story i will be asking chile dasa a few more questions general questions about awakening and some other topics that i hope will be of interest to you as well as um well topics such as mental illness sexual desire what awakening really is and dealing with death and illness i want to apologize for my lack of technical skill in putting this whole thing together um as you can see they're not very sophisticated i have only edited them to edit out interruptions that we had like phones ringing and that sort of thing and i also you know i have to apologize for my inexperience in doing this type of interview it took some time for us to find our feet and necessarily we started off with a lot more storytelling or narrative in describing jhānas early life because he hadn't started a spiritual practice then so as the videos proceed i think you'll find we get much more into the meaning and connection to spiritual practice now i realize for a lot of people this may not be of interest but i have personally gained a lot of insight into the dharma and my own practice and the possibilities are of the sparth by listening to him and i really want to thank him for his generosity and candor in talking to me i think you'll agree that he was incredibly forthcoming um and i found just listening to all the struggles that he's been through really inspiring uh to the to the tune of same as i felt reading you know ayakemo dipama or aloka's books that you know if they can do it with all those difficulties in their life then surely i can um and so i just hope these videos are as interesting and valuable to you as they have been to me and uh may all beings be free of suffering thanks very much and i hope you enjoy them
